validity.recommendation: Change StartCountryOrArea from Russia to Ukraine and add Luhansk Oblast as the start province. Also research the owner split, since Gazprom PJSC at 100 percent is unlikely for a line that starts in Ukraine.
validity.researcher_notes: Country: Novopskov is in the north of Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine, per Ukrainian Wikipedia and Radio Svoboda. The sheet shows Russia for the start country. Occupied Ukraine is still Ukraine. Owner: no document I found states an owner or a split, so no replacement is proposed. The line is real, a gas trunk, and does not overlap another roster row.

validity.recommendation: Keep 878 km. The 388 km in Ukrainian Wikipedia looks like an error, since the end points are about 766 km apart in a straight line. Check the energybase.ru listing by hand.
validity.researcher_notes: The 2022 design institute table gives 878 km for one string of 1200 mm. Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 388 km and rests on a blocked energybase.ru page. The sheet value of 878 km agrees with the design institute table. The same table lists 1200 mm only, while Wikipedia gives 1220 mm, which is why the sheet carries both.

fills.researcher_notes: I found no source dated 2024 or later that says this line is in use. Searches in Russian and Ukrainian on the Novopskov to Mozdok line returned only 2022 reports about the Novopskov hub being taken over. This line runs south into Russia and is not a transit line to Europe, so the 2025 end of transit does not apply to it. The value stays as recorded.

fills.researcher_notes: The sheet says Russia for the start country. Novopskov is in the north of Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine, as stated by Ukrainian Wikipedia and by Radio Svoboda. The corrected start country is Ukraine. Mozdok is in North Ossetia, Russia, which is unchanged.

No operator is recorded and I found no document that names one. The Russian sections are in the Gazprom system. The Novopskov hub is in territory held by Russia since 2022, so naming the Ukrainian system operator would be wrong. I searched in Russian and Ukrainian and read the Ukrainian Wikipedia article and the design institute table. Neither names an operator.
No source found that states who owns this line. Gazprom 100 percent looks too high for a line that starts in Ukraine, but I found no document giving a split. See the owner concern.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No source dated 2024 or later says whether this line is in use. The line runs from the Novopskov hub (occupied by Russia since 2022) south through Rostov and Stavropol to Mozdok. The end of Russian transit through Ukraine on 1 January 2025 does not apply to it. Absence of news is not evidence, so the status is not changed.
